source_caption:
The Son (2022) is a quiet, emotional story about family, guilt, and how hard it is to really understand the people you love. It follows Peter, a successful lawyer in New York who seems to have his life together with a new partner and a newborn baby. But things get complicated when his teenage son Nicholas from his previous marriage starts struggling and suddenly drops out of school.

Nicholas moves in with Peter, and at first it feels like a fresh start might help. Peter does what he can, therapy, support, trying to be present, but he’s also juggling work, a new relationship, and the pressure of being a father again. Meanwhile, Nicholas stays quiet and distant, and it slowly becomes clear that what he’s going through is much deeper than it seems.

As things get heavier, Peter starts looking back at his own childhood and his difficult relationship with his father, wondering if his past mistakes played a role in what’s happening now.

In the end, The Son is really about how complicated parenthood can be. It shows that even when you care and try your best, it doesn’t always fix everything. It’s heartbreaking, honest, and leaves you thinking about the lasting impact families have on each other.

source_details.synopsis: The Son is a 2022 drama film directed by Florian Zeller from a screenplay written by Zeller and Christopher Hampton. It is based on Zeller's 2018 stage play. The film stars Hugh Jackman, Laura Dern, Vanessa Kirby, Zen McGrath, Hugh Quarshie, and Anthony Hopkins. The Son had its world premiere at the 79th Venice International Film Festival on 7 September 2022, and was released for a one-week limited theatrical release in New York City and Los Angeles on 25 November 2022, before a wide release in the United States on 20 January 2023 by Sony Pictures Classics.
